obligations.residual_obligations: ECL profile declaration does not implement in-band ACS ClientHello/ServerHello negotiation. The ACS-Core wire protocol is outside ECL by design and connects through the binding profile ACS-BINDING-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: The comparison is ACS-Core only, not optional profiles.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: DCMP-2 is a different wire protocol; no JSON-RPC 2.0 ACS envelope compatibility is provided. ACS messages connect to DCMP-2 decisions through the binding profile ACS-BINDING-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: A shared request/response concept is not wire compatibility.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ECL does not implement the ACS lifecycle hook names, payloads or negotiated optional hooks. Hook points connect as decision or enforcement points through the binding profile ACS-BINDING-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: ECL execution and authority events are not ACS hook implementations.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ALLOW/DENY have admit/deny analogues; ASK/DEFER have challenge/hold analogues with different semantics. MODIFY is absent and mandatory ACS disposition fields are not supplied; ACS dispositions connect to ECL decisions through the binding profile ACS-BINDING-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: Vocabulary mapping does not establish ACS decision-honoring behavior.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Digest-bound causal predecessors are not an append-only ACS ContextEntry store or published rolling chain head. Context accumulation and IBAC intent evaluation remain deployment work. ECL1N-0178 classifies each input by its source and derivation: actor-controlled context is actor_supplied; intent-alignment judgments are judgment. Either class may only make an outcome stricter (ECL1N-0179). Authenticated authoritative context can be verifiable only with the declared authority, independent validation, freshness, selection, completeness and derivation controls of ECL1N-0178. ACS-BINDING-1 retains and checks native chain heads (AC1-008, AC1-009); it does not implement the context store or IBAC evaluator.
assumptions: Intent is optional in ACS-Core and normative when its IBAC paradigm is chosen.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ECL request identity, retry and expiry semantics support replay control; ACS UUID/timestamp wire fields and Guardian replay rules still need a dedicated adapter and deployment checks.
assumptions: Runtime replay prevention must be enforced; timestamps alone do not provide it.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ECL asymmetric envelopes use a different mechanism from ACS-Core per-session HKDF/HMAC-SHA256. They do not implement that HMAC wire requirement; no blanket strength ranking is inferred.
assumptions: Optional ACS-Crypto has further mechanisms outside this Core-only comparison.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ACS-Core's default-proceed posture on decision failure conflicts with ECL's requirement to fail closed when required proof is missing or invalid. ACS permits a different configured posture; a deployment claiming ACS-BINDING-1 must negotiate deny and configure startup refuse under AC1-006. This stricter binding does not provide the complete ACS decision-honoring implementation. This row is not a gap to implement by allowing fail-open.
assumptions: An ACS deployment may configure a different posture, but the captured Core default must not be silently equated with ECL.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: No ACS system/ping method is specified or implemented, and ACS-BINDING-1 maps none: ECL-1 relies on the decision timeout, after which a Guardian that has not answered is a decision failure that releases nothing (AC1-006).
assumptions: HTTP health endpoints are not the ACS liveness wire method.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: No protocols/MCP ACS wrapper is specified or implemented. An MCP tool gateway connects under the binding profile MCP-GATEWAY-1, and the ACS wrapper under ACS-BINDING-1, both in profiles/.
assumptions: Tool use through an MCP gateway under MCP-GATEWAY-1 is not ACS wrapped-MCP support.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.
